title: The energy conditions and model selection in the local Universe
comment: 15 pages, 15 figures, 4 tables. Published in EPJ-C
summary: The four principal energy conditions (ECs) in general relativity prohibit negative energies, repulsive gravity and superluminal energy flows. One must invoke exotic matter to violate any one of these, yet $Λ$CDM does so quite prominently during inflation and in the epoch of dark energy dominance. In this paper, we carry out model selection between the standard model and the $R_{\rm h}=ct$ universe using a combination of HII galaxy and cosmic chronometer measurements in the local Universe, and directly compare the results to the constraints imposed by the ECs. We find that the latter cosmology is not only strongly favored by these data, with a likelihood of $\sim 92\%$ versus only $\sim 8\%$ for the former, but that its optimized fit is fully compliant with all four ECs, while $Λ$CDM's best fit violates the so-called strong energy condition at $z\lesssim 2$.

AI.tldr: This study compares standard $\Lambda$CDM and $R_{\rm h}=ct$ cosmologies using local Universe data, finding that $R_{\rm h}=ct$ fits significantly better and complies with energy conditions, unlike $\Lambda$CDM that violates the strong energy condition during recent cosmic history.
AI.motivation: Investigate the validity and implications of energy conditions in cosmology, particularly comparing $\Lambda$CDM and the $R_{\rm h}=ct$ universe models.
AI.method: Model selection using HII galaxy and cosmic chronometer data in the local Universe to compare $\Lambda$CDM and $R_{\rm h}=ct$ universe, checking compliance with the four principal energy conditions.
AI.result: The $R_{\rm h}=ct$ universe is strongly favored (~92% likelihood) over $\Lambda$CDM (~8%), with $R_{\rm h}=ct$ fully complying with all four energy conditions while $\Lambda$CDM violates the strong energy condition at redshift $z \lesssim 2$.
AI.conclusion: $R_{\rm h}=ct$ universe provides a better fit to local Universe observational data and respect for fundamental energy conditions in general relativity than $\Lambda$CDM, which requires violation of the strong energy condition at certain epochs.

title: Nebular Fingerprints of a Violent White Dwarf Merger: 3D NLTE Modelling of Type Ia Supernovae
summary: Binary systems composed of two carbon-oxygen white dwarfs (WDs) are a leading progenitor candidate for Type Ia supernovae. One widely discussed scenario is the dynamically driven double-degenerate double-detonation (D$^6$) of a sub-Chandrasekhar-mass WD binary, where detonations are triggered by dynamical interaction. However, some systems are expected to undergo violent mergers, in which the primary ignites through direct carbon ignition as the secondary strikes its surface. We present the first 3D nebular-phase radiative-transfer calculations of a violent merger, using a $1.1 M_\odot$ and $0.7 M_\odot$ sub-Chandrasekhar binary. Our simulations employ a full NLTE (non local thermodynamic equilibrium) treatment of excitation and ionisation, including non-thermal electron contributions. By comparing 1D and 3D realisations, we show that multidimensional modelling improves the ionisation state and reveals features absent from 1D calculations, most notably [O I] from unburned material associated with the secondary. The model reproduces much of the panchromatic spectrum of the normal SN 2021aefx, but underpredicts [Ni II] while producing strong high-ionisation stable-Ni features, illustrating that stable-Ni signatures depend not only on abundance, but also on ionisation state. Although the model does not reproduce the strong [Ar II] and [Ne II] emission observed in the 03fg-like SN 2022pul, our calculations suggest that this event may require a similar merger configuration, involving full disruption of the secondary or a more massive companion with more extensive burning. Finally, viewing-angle variation is substantial, with signatures distinct from D$^6$-like scenarios, suggesting that JWST nebular samples, combined with multidimensional modelling, can discriminate between channels.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first 3D nebular-phase radiative-transfer simulations of violent mergers in sub-Chandrasekhar WD binaries, showing improved spectral predictions over 1D models. The work suggests distinct viewing-angle-dependent signatures and highlights the utility of JWST data for distinguishing Type Ia supernova progenitor scenarios.
AI.motivation: To investigate the detailed nebular-phase signatures of violent mergers in sub-Chandrasekhar-mass carbon-oxygen white dwarf binaries as progenitors of Type Ia supernovae, improving on existing 1D models with 3D radiative-transfer simulations.
AI.method: Performed the first 3D nebular-phase radiative-transfer calculations of a violent WD merger using a $1.1 M_\odot$ and $0.7 M_\odot$ binary system, incorporating full NLTE treatment including non-thermal electron effects; compared 3D results to 1D calculations to evaluate ionisation state and spectral features.
AI.result: 3D models improved ionisation state accuracy and revealed spectral features absent in 1D models, notably [O I] emission from unburned secondary material. The model matched much of the normal SN 2021aefx spectrum but underpredicted [Ni II] and produced strong stable-Ni high-ionisation features. The model did not reproduce strong [Ar II] and [Ne II] seen in 03fg-like SN 2022pul, indicating possibly different merger conditions. Significant viewing-angle effects distinguish violent mergers from D$^6$ scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Multidimensional nebular-phase radiative-transfer modelling is essential to accurately interpret spectra of Type Ia supernovae from violent WD mergers. Viewing-angle dependent spectral signatures can help differentiate between progenitor scenarios like violent mergers and D$^6$ double-detonations. JWST nebular observations combined with 3D models provide a promising path to constrain supernova channels.

title: Dominated-Convergence Failure in Cosmological Perturbation Theory and a Numerical Foundation for BBGKY+ZA
summary: A common ingredient in cosmological perturbation theory (PT) is the expansion of the dark matter overdensity $δ$ in the Lagrangian displacement $s$, which amounts to enforcing mass conservation perturbatively. In Eulerian PT (EPT), that expansion occurs already at the level of the continuity equation; in Lagrangian PT (LPT) it is done in the Poisson equation. We show that the resulting perturbative solutions for $δ$ can diverge not because of the expansion in $s$ per se, but because of an exchange of an infinite sum with a Fourier integral that violates the conditions of Lebesgue's dominated-convergence (DC) theorem. We show that this DC obstruction (DCO) is one clear reason why the convergence of EPT is controlled by advection terms beyond the linear $δ$. The same DCO underlies LPT: LPT's region of validity is the resummation region of a DC-violating series, bounded by shell crossing on one side and severely underdense regions on the other. Effective field theories (EFT) of large-scale structure need to smooth at short scales just to recover from that DCO, independent of whether non-linearities beyond mass conservation are important or not. An alternative is to never expand $δ$ in $s$: instead evolve phase-space cumulants using the BBGKY hierarchy, initialized with the Zel'dovich approximation (ZA). The DCO is then absent by construction, so an EFT of BBGKY can focus on physics beyond mass conservation, which may allow pushing PT beyond shell crossing. The trade-off is the need for a closure relation, for which one can again use the ZA. We provide the building blocks for such a BBGKY+ZA recipe. A bottleneck for implementing it has been the ZA phase-space two-point function $\mathcal{P}$, which we successfully integrate numerically; we then write the higher ZA phase-space correlators needed for closure as products and convolutions of $\mathcal{P}$.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies why standard cosmological perturbation methods diverge due to violating mathematical convergence criteria and proposes a novel approach using BBGKY hierarchy with Zel'dovich approximation to overcome these issues, enabling better modeling of dark matter structure beyond shell crossing.
AI.motivation: Address the divergence problems in perturbative expansions of dark matter overdensity in cosmological perturbation theory and improve methods beyond shell crossing.
AI.method: Analyze the convergence issues of Eulerian and Lagrangian perturbation theories related to Lebesgue's dominated-convergence theorem; propose evolving phase-space cumulants via the BBGKY hierarchy initialized with the Zel'dovich approximation to avoid DC violations; numerically integrate the Zel'dovich approximation phase-space two-point function and express higher correlators as products and convolutions.
AI.result: Showed that divergence arises from violating dominated-convergence conditions rather than the expansion itself; established that effective field theories must smooth short scales due to this; presented a BBGKY+ZA framework that bypasses the DC obstruction and can potentially extend perturbation theory beyond shell crossing with closure relations; successfully integrated the key numerical components for implementation.
AI.conclusion: The DC obstruction fundamentally limits convergence in conventional perturbative expansions of dark matter overdensity, but using BBGKY hierarchy with Zel'dovich approximation overcomes this, offering a path to model nonlinear structure formation beyond current limits without intrinsic divergence issues.

title: The MeerKAT Thousand-Pulsar Polarization Array I: Properties of the Polarization and Rotation Measure Time Series Data
summary: The polarimetry of recent pulsar observations has provided a wealth of observational data with which to test physical theories of emission mechanisms, radiative transfer and even theories that extend beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we have outlined the data analysis of the polarisation time series data of a population of 513 pulsars from the Thousand Pulsar Array observing programme, laying the foundation for building the MeerKAT Thousand-Pulsar Polarization Array as a probe for ultralight Axion-Like Dark Matter (ALDM). From this large dataset we have focused on the temporal trends in the observed polarisation angle (PA) through a measure we call the PA offset, and characterised the trends due to the effects of Faraday Rotation within the interstellar medium and the Earth's ionosphere, as well as generic white and red noise models that are estimated within a Bayesian MCMC analysis. Then, motivated by potential extra contributions to the rotation of the PA that may not be Faraday-like, arising from the proposed ALDM field, we have investigated a derived time dependence for the rotation measure (RM) required to explain the observed PA offset. Comparison of these estimates to RM values that are measured in typical pulsar studies, through a technique known as RM Synthesis, provides a probe of any wavelength-independent contribution to the rotation of the PA. Although we find no evidence for oscillatory behaviour within our dataset's observation timespan, we do find cases of deviation from the usual RM values in several `pulsars of interest', as well as long-term linear trends in the time evolution of Faraday rotation that have been presented in the literature before.

AI.tldr: Analyzed polarisation data of 513 pulsars to explore effects of ultralight Axion-Like Dark Matter on polarisation angle rotation; no ALDM signal found but noted deviations and long-term Faraday rotation trends in some pulsars.
AI.motivation: To use pulsar polarimetry data to test physical theories of emission mechanisms, radiative transfer, and explore potential effects beyond the Standard Model, such as ultralight Axion-Like Dark Matter.
AI.method: Analysis of polarisation time series data from 513 pulsars from the Thousand Pulsar Array, focusing on temporal trends in polarisation angle (PA) offset, Bayesian MCMC modeling of noise and Faraday rotation effects, and comparison of derived rotation measure (RM) time dependence with standard RM values using RM Synthesis.
AI.result: No evidence was found for oscillatory behavior expected from ALDM within the observation timespan, but deviations from typical RM values and long-term linear trends in Faraday rotation were observed in certain pulsars, consistent with previous literature.
AI.conclusion: The study sets a foundation for using the MeerKAT Thousand-Pulsar Polarization Array to probe ultralight Axion-Like Dark Matter, showing no current detection of ALDM-induced signatures but highlighting interesting deviations and trends in Faraday rotation worth further investigation.

title: A Designer's Guide to Lunar Far-Side Interferometer Array: Power Spectrum Measurement and Cosmological Constraints from the Dark Ages
summary: The 21-cm emission line from neutral hydrogen during the cosmic Dark Ages can be a powerful probe of cosmological models and early universe physics. This work provides a quantitative forecast for the design requirements of a lunar far-side interferometer array aimed at measuring the 21-cm power spectrum and constraining inflationary models through the running of the spectral index $α_s$. During the Dark Ages, larger collapsed objects have not yet formed, allowing linear perturbation theory to remain valid down to much smaller scales than is possible in current large-scale structure or CMB surveys. We first validate this linearity assumption by quantifying the contribution of minihalos to the 21-cm signal. We then establish a generalized and flexible analytical framework for the baseline density distribution of interferometers that may consist of an arbitrary number of stations or sub-arrays. Incorporating a realistic noise model, we determine the configurations necessary to reach the detection threshold and demonstrate that distributing the total collecting area into multiple stations can improve the signal-to-noise ratio of the power spectrum at a tunable small scale of interest by up to two orders of magnitude. We then show that a lunar array requires at least $\sim30,000$ probed Fourier modes to achieve a constraint on inflation of $σ(α_s) = 0.034$, a result competitive with the Planck 2018 results and capable of distinguishing between different inflationary scenarios. We quantitatively explain how thermal noise severely erodes modes at high redshifts and small scales -- scales previously considered easily accessible to Dark Ages observations in the literature -- and discuss the prospects for Dark Ages observations as a new and independent probe despite this limitation.

AI.tldr: This paper forecasts design requirements for a lunar far-side interferometer array to measure the 21-cm power spectrum from the cosmic Dark Ages and constrain inflation via the spectral index running. It validates linear theory assumptions, develops an analytical framework for array baselines, and shows that multi-station configurations significantly boost sensitivity. Achieving competitive constraints (σ(α_s)=0.034) requires probing ~30,000 Fourier modes. Thermal noise limits observations at high redshift and small scales, but the method remains a promising independent probe of early universe physics.
AI.motivation: To leverage the 21-cm emission line during the cosmic Dark Ages as a probe for cosmological models and early universe physics, specifically to constrain inflationary models by measuring the spectral index running.
AI.method: Validated linear perturbation theory assumptions by quantifying minihalos' contribution to the 21-cm signal; developed a generalized analytical framework for the baseline density distribution of lunar far-side interferometer arrays; incorporated realistic noise modeling to optimize array configurations; analyzed signal-to-noise improvements by subdividing collecting area into multiple stations; evaluated detection thresholds and Fourier mode requirements for constraining inflation.
AI.result: Demonstrated that distributing total collecting area into multiple stations significantly enhances the power spectrum signal-to-noise ratio by up to two orders of magnitude; established a minimum of ~30,000 Fourier modes are needed for the lunar array to achieve a constraint of σ(α_s) = 0.034 on the running of the spectral index, competitive with Planck 2018 constraints; identified that thermal noise imposes significant limitations on observing high redshift and small scale modes, reducing previously anticipated observational reach; confirmed the viability of Dark Ages 21-cm observations as an independent cosmological probe despite challenges.
AI.conclusion: A lunar far-side interferometer array designed with optimized baseline distributions and multiple stations can effectively measure the 21-cm power spectrum from the Dark Ages to constrain inflationary parameters at competitive precision; however, thermal noise fundamentally limits access to some scales, highlighting the need for careful design and realistic expectations for such observations.

title: Assessing the Relative Importance of Neutrino Matter Interaction Channels in Post-Merger Remnant of Binary Neutron Stars
summary:
Neutron star mergers are amongst the most promising sources for the joint detection of gravitational waves and electromagnetic signals. They are also potential sites for the production of r-process elements and probes of the equation of state of matter above nuclear saturation density. Neutrino-matter interactions during and after merger strongly influence the thermodynamic evolution and composition of the remnant and its outflows, thereby affecting kilonova emission and nucleosynthesis yields. However, existing merger simulations remain limited by significant approximations in the treatment of neutrino transport and interaction rates. In this work, we assess the thermodynamic conditions under which neutrinos decouple from matter and show the effect of charged-current absorption, quasi-elastic scattering on nucleons and nuclei, pair-production processes, and inelastic neutrino-electron scattering for electron neutrinos, electron antineutrinos, and heavy-lepton neutrinos in the different thermodynamical conditions sampled by a simulation using an energy-dependent Monte Carlo neutrino transport.
  We first estimate opacities in the post-merger remnant assuming neutrinos in equilibria with the fluid, and find results consistent with previous studies performed on simulations using a gray two-moment scheme. We note the very distinct regions in which nucleon-nucleon Bremmstrahlung and electron-positron annihilation are active (high and low density regions, respectively). We then evaluate opacities using the actual distribution function of neutrinos within a Monte Carlo simulation. We show greatly increased pair annihilation rates in cold, low-density regions, especially for heavy-lepton neutrinos. We also show that inelastic scattering on electrons, which has not been included in merger simulations so far, makes important contributions to the thermalization of heavy-lepton neutrinos.

AI.tldr: This study uses advanced Monte Carlo simulations to better characterize neutrino interactions in neutron star merger remnants, highlighting important processes affecting neutrino thermalization and emission profiles not captured by prior models.
AI.motivation: Neutron star mergers are crucial for multi-messenger astronomy and nucleosynthesis but current simulations inadequately treat neutrino transport and interactions, limiting understanding of remnant evolution and emitted signals.
AI.method: Used energy-dependent Monte Carlo neutrino transport to assess neutrino decoupling conditions and the effects of neutrino interactions including charged-current absorption, quasi-elastic scattering, pair-production, and inelastic neutrino-electron scattering in post-merger remnants.
AI.result: Found distinct active regions for nucleon-nucleon bremsstrahlung and electron-positron annihilation, identified increased pair annihilation rates in cold, low-density areas for heavy-lepton neutrinos, and demonstrated the significant role of inelastic neutrino-electron scattering in thermalizing heavy-lepton neutrinos, which was previously neglected.
AI.conclusion: Improved neutrino transport modeling reveals nuanced interaction rates and thermalization effects crucial for accurate predictions of remnant thermodynamics, kilonova emissions, and nucleosynthesis yields in neutron star mergers.

title: Model Independent Probe of Variation of Cosmic Opacity with Redshift
comment: 18 pages, 11 figures Accepted for publication in Journal of Astrophysics and Astronomy
summary:
Cosmic opacity may vary spatially due to the inhomogeneous distribution of dust, its grain properties, and the efficiency of photon attenuation. In this work, we present a model independent method to investigate the variation of cosmic opacity with redshift. Using strong gravitational lensing data we construct the opacity independent comoving distance function and we use latest supernovae type Ia (SNe Ia) Pantheon+ data to estimate the opacity dependent comoving distances. Using the distance duality equation, opacity parameter is constrained.
  Our analysis indicates a transparent Universe on average over the redshift range ($0.01 \leq z \leq 2.26137$) of Pantheon+ sample. However, if we split the dataset into subsamples with redshift bins of width $\bigtriangleup z = 0.1$, we find appreciable deviation from the transparency in several redshift intervals. Particularly, in the redshift range $0.3 < z \leq 0.4$, the opacity parameter is $ε= -0.4283^{+0.1914}_{-0.2027}$. The current SNe Ia observations indicate the variation of opacity parameter with redshift. These results may have a significant impact on the values of the cosmological parameters deduced from the SNe Ia observations.

AI.tldr: This study uses gravitational lensing and SNe Ia data to show that cosmic opacity is not uniform across redshifts, with significant deviations detected in certain intervals, implying that cosmic dust and photon attenuation affect cosmological measurements.
AI.motivation: To investigate the potential spatial variation of cosmic opacity caused by inhomogeneous dust distribution and photon attenuation processes, which could affect cosmological parameter estimations.
AI.method: A model-independent approach using strong gravitational lensing data to derive opacity-independent comoving distances, combined with the latest Pantheon+ SNe Ia data for opacity-dependent comoving distances; the opacity parameter is then constrained via the distance duality relation.
AI.result: The analysis suggests that the Universe is transparent on average across the redshift range 0.01 ≤ z ≤ 2.26137, but shows notable deviations in certain redshift bins, especially at 0.3 < z ≤ 0.4 where the opacity parameter significantly deviates from zero.
AI.conclusion: Cosmic opacity varies with redshift, challenging the assumption of a uniformly transparent Universe and potentially impacting the accuracy of cosmological parameters derived from SNe Ia observations.

title: Recoil-regulated extreme mass-ratio inspirals in AGN disks
summary: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are among the primary targets of future space-based gravitational-wave observatories, such as LISA, TianQin, and Taiji. Active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks provide a gas-rich environment in which stellar-mass black holes can migrate toward central supermassive black holes and form EMRIs. Previous studies of this ``wet'' channel have largely neglected stellar interactions within the disk. Here we show that binary formation, hierarchical mergers, and recoil kicks fundamentally regulate wet EMRI formation in AGN disks. Using semi-analytical AGN disk models combined with Monte Carlo simulations across supermassive black hole masses of $10^5$--$10^7M_\odot$ and Eddington ratios of $10^{-3}$-1, we find that recoil kicks from mergers and binary--single interactions repeatedly lift stellar-mass black holes out of the disk plane, temporarily interrupting migration and strongly suppressing EMRI formation in much of parameter space. Detectable EMRIs are therefore preferentially produced in young AGNs, typically within $\sim$ 10-20Myr of disk formation, and often involve merger-grown secondary black holes. We predict LISA detection rates of $\sim$ 1-30yr$^{-1}$, with the observable population dominated by low-mass AGNs and sensitive to the poorly constrained demographics of faint active nuclei. Our results identify stellar interactions as a key ingredient in the evolution of compact objects in AGN disks and show that future EMRI observations can probe both AGN disk physics and the low-mass AGN population.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that stellar interactions strongly influence EMRI formation in AGN disks, leading to suppression except in young AGNs. It predicts detectable EMRIs mainly from low-mass AGNs and highlights EMRIs as probes of AGN disk physics and faint AGN populations.
AI.motivation: To understand the impact of stellar interactions on the formation of extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) in active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks, which have been previously neglected in studies of the 'wet' channel of EMRI formation.
AI.method: The study uses semi-analytical models of AGN disks combined with Monte Carlo simulations over a range of supermassive black hole masses ($10^5$--$10^7M_\odot$) and Eddington ratios ($10^{-3}$ to 1).
AI.result: Recoil kicks from mergers and binary-single interactions lift stellar-mass black holes out of the disk plane, interrupting migration and suppressing EMRI formation across much of the parameter space. Detectable EMRIs are more likely in young AGNs within ~10-20 Myr of disk formation and often involve merger-grown secondaries. Predicted LISA detection rates are ~1-30 per year, dominated by low-mass AGNs and depending on demographics of faint active nuclei.
AI.conclusion: Stellar interactions such as binary formation, hierarchical mergers, and recoil kicks critically regulate the formation of wet EMRIs in AGN disks. Future EMRI observations can probe AGN disk physics and the population of low-mass AGNs.

title: The observer power spectrum for lightcone statistics, integrated relativistic observables and wide angle effects
summary: The statistics of large-scale structure are naturally described by power spectra in Fourier space. For fields on spatial hypersurfaces, translational invariance makes different Fourier modes uncorrelated and the power spectrum diagonal. Cosmological observables, however, are measured on our past lightcone, where wide-angle effects, radial evolution and integrated effects such as lensing break this symmetry: Fourier-space statistics become non-diagonal, with mode-mixing generated by the geometry of the lightcone itself. We define a more natural observer power spectrum by Fourier transforming over observer positions on a spatial hypersurface with fixed lightcone coordinates, rather than over source positions on a single lightcone. This forms a field on the observer hypersurface with a moveable light-ray leg. Statistical homogeneity of the observer hypersurface implies that this spectrum is diagonal for any observable, whether local or integrated and does not suffer from mode-mixing. We show how the various two-point statistics used in large-scale structure analysis are each recovered as projections of the observer spectrum. This extends directly to higher-order statistics. We illustrate it by constructing the relativistic kernel for the observed galaxy number count fluctuation, including density, redshift-space distortions, Doppler, lensing magnification, and integrated Sachs-Wolfe contributions.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an observer power spectrum approach that restores diagonality in Fourier-space statistics of cosmological observables on the lightcone, overcoming mode-mixing due to geometric effects, and unifies various two-point and higher-order statistics under a common framework.
AI.motivation: To address the mode-mixing problem in Fourier-space statistics of cosmological observables measured on the past lightcone, where translational invariance is broken due to wide-angle effects, radial evolution, and integrated phenomena like lensing.
AI.method: Define an observer power spectrum by Fourier transforming over observer positions on a spatial hypersurface with fixed lightcone coordinates, creating a field on the observer hypersurface with a moveable light-ray leg, and demonstrating that its statistical homogeneity ensures a diagonal spectrum without mode-mixing.
AI.result: The observer power spectrum is diagonal for any observable, including local and integrated effects, avoiding mode-mixing; various two-point statistics are recoverable as projections of this spectrum and the approach extends to higher-order statistics. A relativistic kernel for the observed galaxy number count fluctuation including multiple effects is constructed.
AI.conclusion: The proposed observer power spectrum framework resolves mode-mixing issues inherent to traditional Fourier-space statistics on the past lightcone by leveraging statistical homogeneity on the observer hypersurface, leading to diagonal power spectra for a broad range of cosmological observables and enabling consistent treatment of higher-order statistics.

title: Sub-luminous Type IIP SN 2024abfl as a result of a significantly low energy Fe-core collapse
comment: Accepted in the ApJ. (21 pages, 14 figures)
summary: We present extensive, well-sampled multiwavelength photometric and low-resolution optical spectroscopic observations of the low-luminosity Type IIP supernova SN 2024abfl. SN 2024abfl is found to be at the faintest end of Type IIP supernovae with unprecedented flat (0.1 mag/ 100 day) plateau evolution and a mid-plateau absolute magnitude of Mv~-13.8 mag, placing it among one of the faintest Type IIP supernovae discovered to date. SN 2024abfl is adjacent to SN 2018zd in the same host NGC~2146. Using various SN distance measurement probes, we provide independent estimates of the debated distance to the host NGC 2146 (7-9 Mpc). Spectral evolution of SN 2024abfl is found to be similar to other SNe spectra of this subclass but with very narrow line profiles, indicating moderately low expansion velocities of the ejecta. Detailed 1-D hydrodynamical modeling suggests a compact progenitor with an upper limit of 10 Msun, fairly consistent with the directly detected progenitor estimates. It exploded with very low-energy 0.05 foe or less with a very low nickel mass of 0.003 Msun, consistent with the observed parameters. These parameters provide important constraints on the nature of low-energy core-collapse explosions. We discuss possible progenitor scenarios and compare SN 2024abfl with other low-luminosity Type IIP supernovae.

AI.tldr: This study presents detailed observations and modeling of the extremely faint Type IIP supernova SN 2024abfl, revealing a low-mass, compact progenitor and low-energy explosion, which help constrain theories on low-luminosity core-collapse supernovae.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature of low-energy core-collapse supernovae, especially at the faintest end of the Type IIP subclass, by studying SN 2024abfl.
AI.method: Multiwavelength photometric and low-resolution optical spectroscopic observations combined with 1-D hydrodynamical modeling and distance measurements to the host galaxy NGC 2146.
AI.result: SN 2024abfl shows unprecedented flat plateau evolution at a very faint absolute magnitude, very low expansion velocities, and low explosion energy and nickel mass; the progenitor is compact with an upper mass limit around 10 Msun.
AI.conclusion: The observed and modeled parameters of SN 2024abfl provide valuable constraints on the progenitor properties and explosion mechanisms of low-luminosity Type IIP supernovae, supporting a scenario involving a compact, low-mass star undergoing a low-energy core-collapse.

title: Exploring the High-Redshift 21-cm Signal via Self-Consistent Simulations using Artificial Neural Network Emulation
summary: We present a novel, self-consistent, semi-numeric Cosmic Dawn (CD) simulation in which small-scale star formation (SF) is calibrated to the \emph{AEOS} and \emph{Renaissance} hydrodynamic simulations. SF proceeds within dark matter (DM) halos via neural network emulation while considering large-scale fluctuations in density and feedback. We translate the resulting 3D distribution of galaxies into predictions for the 21-cm brightness temperature, \Tb, and power spectrum, \PS. We simulate several unique realizations to study the impact of varying astrophysics on \Tb, finding that more efficient Population II (PopII) SF largely yields stronger Lyman-$α$ coupling, resulting in a shallower and wider absorption trough. However, we find that PopII SF dominates \PS\ at $z \lesssim 20$ and on smaller scales at intermediate redshifts ($k \gtrsim 0.2\ \mathrm{Mpc^{-1}}$ at $z \simeq 34-20$) while Population III (PopIII) SF dominates \PS\ at $z\gtrsim34$ and on larger scales at intermediate redshifts. Compared with previous works, we find that the combination of hydrodynamic SF calibration, a critical halo mass for SF considering \Htwo\ self-shielding, and stochastic DM halo merger histories results in both earlier SF and higher SF rates across CD. Further, we find that the delay period separating PopIII and PopII SF (\tdelay) significantly impacts \Tb, and that one must include DM halo merger histories to properly account for this transition. Finally, we find our fiducial \Tb\ to be detectable at $z\lesssim25$ with 1080 hours of HERA observations under moderate foreground assumptions, and the lack of such a detection at $z \gtrsim 20$ would suggest \tdelay\ $\gtrsim$ 30 Myr.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an advanced Cosmic Dawn simulation calibrated to hydrodynamic data and neural networks, showing how star formation variations affect 21-cm signals, with implications for detection by HERA and constraints on cosmic star formation transitions.
AI.motivation: To improve Cosmic Dawn simulations by calibrating small-scale star formation with hydrodynamic simulations and to explore the impact of astrophysical variations on 21-cm signals.
AI.method: Develop a semi-numeric Cosmic Dawn simulation integrating neural network emulation of star formation within dark matter halos, calibrated to AEOS and Renaissance hydrodynamic simulations, including large-scale density fluctuations and feedback; simulate multiple realizations; generate 3D galaxy distributions translating into 21-cm brightness temperature and power spectrum predictions.
AI.result: Efficient PopII star formation yields stronger Lyman-α coupling and alters 21-cm absorption features; PopII dominates power spectrum at lower redshifts and smaller scales, while PopIII dominates at higher redshifts and larger scales; calibration with hydrodynamic SF, critical halo mass considering H2 self-shielding, and stochastic DM merger histories advance star formation timing and rates; delay between PopIII and PopII SF significantly affects signals; 21-cm signal detectable at z < 25 with HERA, and nondetection at z > 20 implies a delay > 30 Myr.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating hydrodynamic calibration, H2 self-shielding, and DM merger histories in Cosmic Dawn simulations significantly improves the modeling of star formation timing and rates, affecting 21-cm signal predictions; observational detection thresholds can constrain the PopIII to PopII transition delay.

title: The Impact of the New $^{59}$Fe Decay Rates on $^{60}$Fe and $^{26}$Al Nucleosynthesis in Massive Stars
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)
summary: The diffuse $γ$-ray emission from short-lived radioactive $^{26}$Al and $^{60}$Fe provides a direct probe of ongoing nucleosynthesis in the Galaxy. However, theoretical models have long struggled to reproduce the observed $^{60}$Fe/$^{26}$Al flux ratio, typically predicting values significantly higher than constraints derived from INTEGRAL/SPI observations. In this work, we investigate the impact of the recently measured, temperature-dependent stellar $β^-$ decay rate of $^{59}$Fe on the nucleosynthesis of these isotopes. We compute a grid of non-rotating massive star models ($14$-$80$ M$_\odot$) at solar metallicity using the MESA code, coupled with a rigorous numerical resolution analysis. We find that the updated rate significantly suppresses the net production of $^{60}$Fe by approximately 0.28 dex ($\sim 47\%$) compared to models using LMP theoretical rates, while leaving $^{26}$Al yields virtually unchanged. This reduction is primarily driven by the enhanced $β^-$ decay during convective carbon shell burning. Integrating these yields over a standard Salpeter Initial Mass Function, we predict a Galactic flux ratio of $\sim 0.18$, which is in excellent agreement with the observed value of $0.184 \pm 0.042$. Furthermore, this ratio exhibits a weak dependence on the IMF slope. Our results indicate that the updated nuclear physics input significantly alleviates the long-standing $^{60}$Fe overproduction problem, bringing theoretical predictions into much closer alignment with current Galactic observations.

AI.tldr: Updating the $^{59}$Fe decay rate in massive star models reduces $^{60}$Fe production by ~47%, bringing the predicted $^{60}$Fe/$^{26}$Al flux ratio into excellent agreement with observed Galactic values, thus resolving a key discrepancy in nucleosynthesis modeling.
AI.motivation: Theoretical models have struggled to reproduce the observed Galactic flux ratio of $^{60}$Fe/$^{26}$Al, often predicting significantly higher values than those measured by INTEGRAL/SPI, indicating a discrepancy in nucleosynthesis modeling.
AI.method: A grid of non-rotating massive star models (14–80 M☉) at solar metallicity was computed using the MESA code, incorporating the recently measured temperature-dependent $β^-$ decay rate of $^{59}$Fe, along with a rigorous numerical resolution analysis; yields were integrated over a Salpeter Initial Mass Function to predict Galactic flux ratios.
AI.result: The updated temperature-dependent $β^-$ decay rate of $^{59}$Fe reduces net $^{60}$Fe production by approximately 47% compared to previous models, with $^{26}$Al yields remaining nearly unchanged, resulting in a predicted Galactic $^{60}$Fe/$^{26}$Al flux ratio of ~0.18 that closely matches observed values and shows weak dependence on IMF slope.
AI.conclusion: The inclusion of the updated stellar $β^-$ decay rate for $^{59}$Fe in nucleosynthesis models resolves the long-standing $^{60}$Fe overproduction problem, aligning theoretical predictions of the $^{60}$Fe/$^{26}$Al flux ratio with current Galactic observations.

title: Cosmo-PINN: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Cosmological Reconstruction
summary: We introduce Cosmo-PINN, a Physics-Informed Neural Network for reconstruction of the cosmological theory. In this work we demonstrate the application of the Cosmo-PINN in the reconstruction of the dark energy equation of state parameter $w_{DE}\left( z\right) $ directly from late-time cosmological observations. This framework overcomes the main limitation shared by Gaussian Process and Artificial Neural Network reconstruction approaches, where the recovered solution is driven by the data and it is not necessarily true that it is physically consistent, by embedding the cosmological constraints directly into the loss function as hard constraints, ensuring that the reconstructed quantities satisfy the physical laws at every point during the training. For the training of the network, we employed background data, and specifically the Baryon Acoustic Oscillation from DESI DR2, the Cosmic Chronometers and three different Supernova compilations, while we simultaneously introduce the cosmological parameters $H_{0},~Ω_{m0}$ and $r_{\mathrm{drag}}$ as trained parameters. The reconstruction shows that the trained $w_{DE}\left( z\right) $ crosses the phantom divide within the redshift range $z=0.27-0.42$ in agreement with the value obtained by the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder model. In the quintessence scenario, for large redshifts the dark energy $Ω_{DE}\left( z\right) $ provides a pressureless nonzero contribution to the cosmological fluid suggesting a unified scenario. Finally, we demonstrate the significance of imposing the physical constraints within the loss function by comparing the Cosmo-PINN reconstruction against a purely data-driven neural network with the same architecture.

AI.tldr: Cosmo-PINN, a Physics-Informed Neural Network trained on cosmological data with embedded physical constraints, reconstructs the dark energy equation of state parameter accurately and physically consistently, outperforming data-driven approaches.
AI.motivation: Existing reconstruction methods for the dark energy equation of state parameter driven primarily by data may yield solutions that are not physically consistent.
AI.method: Cosmo-PINN, a Physics-Informed Neural Network embedding cosmological constraints as hard constraints in the loss function, trained on late-time cosmological background data including Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (DESI DR2), Cosmic Chronometers, and Supernova compilations, while simultaneously training cosmological parameters $H_0, \Omega_{m0}$, and $r_{drag}$.
AI.result: The reconstructed dark energy equation of state parameter $w_{DE}(z)$ crosses the phantom divide at redshifts $z=0.27-0.42$ consistent with the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder model, and at large redshifts the dark energy density $\Omega_{DE}(z)$ behaves as a pressureless component suggesting a unified cosmological fluid scenario.
AI.conclusion: Embedding physical laws as hard constraints in the loss function during neural network training ensures physically consistent reconstruction of cosmological quantities, outperforming purely data-driven methods.

title: A Note on QPE Timing: False Alarms in O-C
summary: O-C timing analysis is a useful diagnostic tool for quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs), but their interpretation depends sensitively on the integer cycle number assigned to each eruption. In this note, we show that even a small mismatch in the cycle number, $N_{\rm cyc}$, can produce large false signals in O-C diagrams, and \emph{a universal feature of these false signals is a large in-phase sinusoidal modulation between even and odd eruptions.} Therefore, uncertainties in $N_{\rm cyc}$ must be inferred or marginalized over before physical interpretations are attached to O-C. We then apply both O-C and EMRI+disk to GSN 069 and eRO-QPE2. For GSN 069, the timing data favor an anti-phase modulation in even and odd eruptions, consistent with apsidal precession in a low-eccetricity EMRI crossing an equatorial disk. For eRO-QPE2, the data are well described by a near-circular EMRI and a precessing disk.

AI.tldr: Incorrect cycle numbering in QPE timing analyses causes false signals in O-C diagrams. After correcting for this, GSN 069 shows signals consistent with an eccentric EMRI-disk interaction, while eRO-QPE2 fits a circular EMRI with a precessing disk.
AI.motivation: Interpreting O-C timing data of QPEs depends critically on correctly assigning the integer cycle number to each eruption. Misassignments can induce misleading signals that complicate the understanding of the physical processes underlying QPEs.
AI.method: The authors use O-C timing analysis coupled with EMRI+disk modeling to analyze quasi-periodic eruptions. They examine the effect of mismatching the integer cycle number on O-C diagrams and apply their methodology to observational data from GSN 069 and eRO-QPE2.
AI.result: They find that even small mismatches in the cycle number produce large false sinusoidal modulations in O-C diagrams, specifically an in-phase pattern between even and odd eruptions. For GSN 069, the timing favors an anti-phase modulation indicative of apsidal precession in an EMRI crossing a disk, and for eRO-QPE2, the observations align with a near-circular EMRI and precessing disk model.
AI.conclusion: Small errors in assigning integer cycle numbers to QPEs lead to false signals in O-C diagrams, characterized by a large in-phase sinusoidal modulation between even and odd eruptions. Accurate interpretation requires accounting for these uncertainties. Applied to GSN 069, the analysis supports an anti-phase modulation due to apsidal precession in a low-eccentricity EMRI-disk system, while for eRO-QPE2, the data indicates a near-circular EMRI with a precessing disk.

title: Signals from the early Universe: a comprehensive search for primordial features in Planck CMB datasets
summary: We investigate the presence of primordial oscillatory features in measurements of CMB anisotropies through a systematic comparison of phenomenological templates. Building upon previous searches for primordial features using Planck data, we compare the full PR3 legacy release with the PR4 (NPIPE) processing to assess how the results depend on the choice of CMB maps and likelihood framework. To maximise our sensitivity to rapidly varying oscillatory signals, we employ unbinned likelihoods. We find that several previously reported indications of oscillatory structure persist across different analyses, although none attains global statistical significance. Furthermore, some anomalies reported in earlier studies are substantially reduced when updated to the new versions of the CamSpec likelihood using Planck PR4 products. For all templates considered, we identify a small number of frequencies in the range $ω\sim 10-100$ that improve the fit to the CMB data by up to $Δχ^2 \simeq -10$ to $-15$ relative to the featureless reference model. However, this improvement is not supported by a Bayesian model comparison. The inclusion of three or four additional parameters can reduces the overall predictability of the feature models and leads to an Occam penalty. Finally, after properly accounting for the look-elsewhere effect, the significance of the preferred frequencies is reduced, corresponding to a global statistical significance of at most $2.6σ$. We present forecasts for forthcoming CMB experiments, highlighting the decisive role of next-generation polarisation measurements in distinguishing genuine primordial oscillations from statistical fluctuations and modelling systematics. The upper bounds or uncertainties on the feature amplitudes, expected from the combination of SO and LiteBIRD, improve by more than one order of magnitude.

AI.tldr: This paper assesses primordial oscillatory features in CMB anisotropies using Planck data, finding no statistically significant evidence after corrections for model complexity and multiple testing. Next-generation CMB polarization experiments promise substantial improvements in testing these models.
AI.motivation: The study aims to investigate the presence of primordial oscillatory features in CMB anisotropies to understand early universe physics better.
AI.method: They conduct a systematic comparison of phenomenological templates applied to Planck PR3 and PR4 data, utilizing unbinned likelihoods to enhance sensitivity to rapidly varying oscillatory signals and employing updated likelihood frameworks such as CamSpec with the latest Planck products.
AI.result: Several indications of oscillatory features are observed across analyses but lack global statistical significance after accounting for the look-elsewhere effect and Bayesian model comparison. Some previously reported anomalies are diminished with updated data versions. The improvement in fit is accompanied by model complexity penalties. Future CMB polarization measurements are forecasted to significantly improve constraints on these features.
AI.conclusion: Though some frequencies improve the fit to CMB data, no statistically significant evidence for primordial oscillatory features is found after rigorous evaluation. Upcoming next-generation CMB experiments, especially using polarization data, will be critical in verifying the existence of such features or discerning them from statistical/systematic artifacts.

title: From reflection to scattering: polarimetric signatures of funnel-type outflows. Modeling obscured ultraluminous X-ray sources
summary: Super-Eddington accretion onto compact objects is expected to produce optically thick outflows with a funnel-shaped cavity that may collimate the emission. At inclinations higher than the grazing angle of the funnel, the central source is obscured. Accordingly, the observed emission is dominated by scattered and reflected radiation, which can therefore be strongly polarized. The detection of strong X-ray polarization in the Galactic X-ray binary Cygnus X-3 provides the first direct probe of this geometry. In this work, we present a systematic study of the inclination-dependent radiative signatures of such systems using a combination of semi-analytical methods and Monte Carlo simulations. Our treatment explicitly accounts for multiple scatterings and demonstrates that both the polarization degree and the degree of collimation are highly sensitive to the albedo of the funnel surface. We find that a low albedo (significant absorption) is essential for producing high polarization, yet it simultaneously suppresses the collimation of the emission. Conversely, a high-albedo medium (nearly pure scattering) can modestly collimate radiation, but at the cost of substantially reducing the polarization degree. We discuss our results in the context of Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer observations of Cygnus X-3 and propose a physical scenario for its spectral state transitions, considering a combination of reflection from the funnel surface and scattering by a diffuse medium above the funnel. Our model provides a general framework for interpreting X-ray polarimetric signatures of obscured accretors.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how super-Eddington accretion produces funnel-shaped outflows whose emission properties depend on inclination and funnel surface albedo, using semi-analytical and Monte Carlo techniques, explaining recent Cygnus X-3 X-ray polarization observations with a model of reflection and scattering in the funnel environment.
AI.motivation: The study is motivated by the need to understand the geometry and emission properties of super-Eddington accretion onto compact objects, particularly in light of recent X-ray polarization observations of Cygnus X-3.
AI.method: The paper employs a combination of semi-analytical methods and Monte Carlo simulations to systematically study inclination-dependent radiative signatures in systems with funnel-shaped outflows, explicitly accounting for multiple scatterings.
AI.result: Results indicate that the degree of polarization and collimation of emitted radiation are highly sensitive to the albedo of the funnel surface: low albedo enhances polarization but reduces collimation, while high albedo improves collimation but diminishes polarization. A physical model is proposed explaining spectral state transitions via reflection and scattering mechanisms.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that X-ray polarization measurements can provide critical insights into the geometry and physical conditions of super-Eddington accretors, offering a general framework to interpret polarimetric signatures of obscured compact objects.

title: Efficient computation of the galaxy angular bispectrum in redshift space
comment: 28 pages, 7 figures. Prepared to submit to JCAP. Comments are welcome
summary: Efficient computation of the angular bispectrum is an essential part of modelling large-scale structure observations, but it still remains an extremely challenging task. In this work, we compute the tree-level, unequal-time angular bispectrum in both real and redshift space. By deriving full-sky results, we show that the bispectrum can be expressed as a sum of products of two angular power spectra, enabling the use of our recently developed flat-sky approximation to enhance computational efficiency significantly. This flat-sky formalism preserves key line-of-sight mode information while discarding extraneous full-sky contributions. We validate our approach by comparing it with direct full-sky integration, finding excellent agreement across a wide range of scales and redshifts for all bispectrum configurations. At redshift $z = 1$, we achieve sub-percent agreement (for multipoles $\ell \gtrsim 5$) between full-sky and flat-sky results for equilateral, squeezed, and folded configurations, using narrow Gaussian radial window functions ($σ_z = 0.01$) in both equal-time and unequal-time scenarios. On small scales, where direct full-sky integration becomes computationally prohibitive, our results align with the Limber approximation (where applicable), confirming the robustness and accuracy of our implementation. To facilitate future studies, we provide a \texttt{Python} implementation of our results, which is publicly available on \texttt{GitHub}.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a computationally efficient flat-sky method to calculate the angular bispectrum in large-scale structure observations, maintaining accuracy comparable to full-sky methods and providing validated Python code for future research.
AI.motivation: Efficient computation of the angular bispectrum is crucial for modeling large-scale structure observations but remains computationally challenging.
AI.method: Derived full-sky expressions for the tree-level, unequal-time angular bispectrum in real and redshift space, expressed as sums of products of two angular power spectra; utilized a flat-sky approximation to significantly improve computational efficiency while preserving key line-of-sight information; validated against direct full-sky integration and compared to Limber approximation on small scales.
AI.result: Achieved sub-percent agreement between full-sky and flat-sky results at redshift z=1 for multiple bispectrum configurations across a broad multipole range; confirmed robustness and accuracy on small scales; provided publicly available Python implementation on GitHub.
AI.conclusion: The flat-sky approximation effectively reproduces full-sky angular bispectrum calculations with high accuracy and greatly enhanced computational efficiency, enabling practical modeling of large-scale structure bispectrum in both real and redshift space for various configurations and redshifts.

title: Time-Domain Deep Learning for Pairwise Identification of Strongly Lensed Gravitational-Wave Candidates
summary: As gravitational wave (GW) catalogs continue to expand, exhaustive Bayesian comparisons of candidate event pairs become increasingly computationally expensive, which motivates the development of fast prescreening methods for strongly lensed GW searches. We formulate lensed-pair identification as a binary verification problem using two preprocessed strain segments. To address this task, we propose Physics-Inspired ResNet (PI-ResNet), a Siamese one-dimensional residual network for pairwise GW candidate classification. Unlike spectrogram-based prescreening approaches, PI-ResNet operates directly on whitened time-domain strain data and avoids an intermediate time--frequency image representation. A shared residual backbone with Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) modules encodes the two input segments, and the paired embeddings are compared through absolute feature differences and Hadamard-product interactions. We train and evaluate the model using simulated GW signals from binary black hole mergers lensed by point-mass (PM) and singular isothermal sphere (SIS) lenses, injected into simulated LIGO and Einstein Telescope (ET) detector noise. Under ET design noise, PI-ResNet achieves accuracies of $95.60\%$ for SIS lenses and $93.80\%$ for PM lenses, while maintaining $84.03\%$ and $78.25\%$ accuracy under simulated LIGO H1--L1 Gaussian noise. These results suggest that direct learning from 1D strain data provides an efficient and physically motivated preselection statistic for candidate lensed GW pairs, while also indicating the need for detector-domain adaptation.

AI.tldr: The study introduces PI-ResNet, a physics-inspired Siamese neural network that directly classifies pairs of gravitational wave signals from time-domain strain data to identify strongly lensed events, achieving high accuracy in simulated detector noise and providing a fast preselection tool to reduce computational challenges in gravitational wave lensing searches.
AI.motivation: To overcome the increasing computational cost of exhaustive Bayesian comparisons in expanding gravitational wave catalogs, fast and effective prescreening methods are needed for identifying strongly lensed gravitational wave candidate pairs.
AI.method: We proposed PI-ResNet, a Siamese one-dimensional residual neural network with Squeeze-and-Excitation modules that operates on whitened time-domain gravitational wave strain data, encoding paired inputs and classifying them via feature differences and Hadamard-product interactions; the model was trained and tested on simulated binary black hole merger signals lensed by point-mass and singular isothermal sphere lenses injected into simulated LIGO and Einstein Telescope noise.
AI.result: PI-ResNet achieved up to 95.60% accuracy for singular isothermal sphere lenses and 93.80% for point-mass lenses under Einstein Telescope noise, and maintained 84.03% and 78.25% accuracy respectively under simulated LIGO H1-L1 Gaussian noise, demonstrating effective direct classification from 1D strain data with some need for adaptation across detector noise domains.
AI.conclusion: PI-ResNet efficiently identifies strongly lensed gravitational wave candidate pairs directly from time-domain strain data, achieving high accuracy across different simulated detector noises, especially Einstein Telescope noise, thereby providing a computationally effective preselection method for gravitational wave lensing.

title: Late-time Quantum Vacuum Decay and its Cosmological Implications
summary: The existence of a landscape of metastable vacua raises the possibility that our Universe may have undergone quantum vacuum decay at late times. This work explores how such a transition can be tested with cosmological observables, focusing on precision distance measurements and cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies. A set of phenomenological models is constructed in which late-time quantum tunneling changes the vacuum energy and may convert a subcomponent of dark matter into dark radiation, possibly accompanied by domain-wall production. The resulting expansion histories are compared with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation data; supernova distance measurements from DES-Dovekie, Pantheon+, and Union3; and a compressed CMB likelihood. For quantum-tunneling models, current cosmological distance measurements still allow a 50% decrease in the total vacuum energy for a transition redshift $z_t<1$. The model with dark-matter conversion and domain-wall production provides a good fit to resolve the tension between cosmological observables and the $Λ$CDM model, with a preferred transition around $z_t \sim 7$ and about 10% of dark matter participating in the transition. Additionally, CMB anisotropy constraints from bubble nucleation and the associated domain-wall network are derived and shown to strongly restrict slow or sparse late transitions. Applied to the minimal quantum-tunneling model, these constraints allow an $\mathcal{O}(10\%)$ decrease in the total vacuum energy for a transition redshift $z_t$ of order unity. For nonminimal models, dark-matter-density-dependent tunneling can proceed rapidly enough to evade such bounds. These results demonstrate that late-time quantum vacuum decay is a testable cosmological phenomenon and provide a concrete observational handle on metastable-vacuum physics motivated by landscape scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper develops and tests models of late-time quantum vacuum decay using cosmological observations, finding that such transitions can be consistent with current data and may relieve tensions in ΛCDM, thereby offering observational access to metastable vacuum physics.
AI.motivation: To explore the possibility and observational consequences of late-time quantum vacuum decay within the metastable vacuum landscape, addressing its testability with cosmological data.
AI.method: Construction of phenomenological models involving quantum tunneling altering vacuum energy and converting dark matter to dark radiation, followed by comparison of resulting expansion histories with multiple cosmological datasets including DESI DR2 BAO, supernova distance measurements, and compressed CMB likelihood; derivation of CMB anisotropy constraints from bubble nucleation and domain-wall networks.
AI.result: Current cosmological distance measurements permit significant late-time decreases (up to 50%) in vacuum energy for certain redshifts; models including dark-matter conversion and domain-wall production can alleviate tensions with ΛCDM and prefer transitions around redshift ~7 with ~10% dark matter involvement; CMB anisotropy constraints limit slow or sparse transitions but allow order 10% vacuum energy decreases at late times; nonminimal tunneling models can evade these bounds due to rapid transitions.
AI.conclusion: Late-time quantum vacuum decay is a testable phenomenon in cosmology, with observational signatures in distance measurements and CMB anisotropies, providing a novel probe into metastable-vacuum physics inspired by theoretical landscape scenarios.

title: Enhanced All-Distance Equi-Zenith Angle Method for Cosmic-Ray Anisotropy Measurement
comment: 16 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D
summary: Long-term observations indicate that the relative intensity of cosmic-ray anisotropy remains below $0.1\%$ for energies less than $\sim 1$ PeV. Measuring such faint signals poses a significant challenge in data analysis, requiring careful removal of instrumental and atmospheric artifacts. The all-distance equi-zenith angle method is widely employed to extract cosmic-ray anisotropies, as it effectively suppresses the instantaneous variations arising from the instrument and atmosphere. \textcolor{black}{However, instability in the detector efficiency makes precise measurements of anisotropy challenging with this method.} In this work, we present an enhanced all-distance equi-zenith angle method for cosmic-ray anisotropy measurement. Unlike previous implementations, our improved approach enables the simultaneous measurement of anisotropies over multiple time frames and allows the detection efficiency to be determined directly from the data. This feature makes the method especially suitable for applications where the detector array does not operate with long-term stability\textcolor{black}{, and thus allows for the measurement of anisotropy with high-precision}. Moreover, our enhanced method is also feasible when the data do not span complete tropical years.

AI.tldr: An improved analysis method for cosmic-ray anisotropy allows precise measurements despite detector instability and incomplete data periods, by simultaneously analyzing multiple time frames and extracting efficiency directly from data.
AI.motivation: Measuring faint cosmic-ray anisotropy signals below 0.1% intensity at energies less than ~1 PeV is challenged by instrumental and atmospheric artifacts, and detector efficiency instability.
AI.method: An enhanced all-distance equi-zenith angle method that enables simultaneous multi-time-frame anisotropy measurement and directly determines detection efficiency from data, improving precision in unstable detector conditions.
AI.result: The improved method achieves high-precision anisotropy measurements even with unstable detector efficiency and incomplete tropical year data coverage.
AI.conclusion: The presented enhanced method effectively overcomes challenges of detector instability and incomplete data, enabling precise cosmic-ray anisotropy measurements under previously difficult conditions.

title: Augmented Correlation Functions for Spectroscopic Galaxy Surveys
summary: Galaxy redshift surveys encode a wealth of information generated by nonlinear gravitational evolution, galaxy bias, and redshift-space distortions, only part of which is accessible through standard two-point statistics. Motivated by the need for flexible and computationally efficient alternatives, we introduce the augmented correlation function, a general framework in which an arbitrary transformation of the galaxy field defines additional ``latent'' dimensions that extend the standard two-point correlation function and isolate clustering properties averaged out in conventional analyses. As a proof of concept, we study a latent variable constructed from the pairwise gradient of the inverse Laplacian of the galaxy density field, showing that the resulting statistics naturally distinguish clustering regimes associated with infalling and outflowing pairs. Using Fisher forecasts based on $z=1$ halo catalogues from the Quijote simulations within $νΛ\mathrm{CDM}$ cosmology, we find that the augmented correlation systematically yields tighter constraints on all cosmological parameters considered. Although these improvements should be regarded as indicative given the exploratory nature of the analysis and the limitations of Fisher forecasts and simulations, our results demonstrate the potential of augmented correlations as a flexible framework for extracting additional information from spectroscopic galaxy surveys.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the augmented correlation function to capture extra clustering information beyond standard two-point statistics in galaxy surveys, showing improved cosmological parameter constraints from simulations, highlighting a promising new tool for spectroscopic data analysis.
AI.motivation: Standard two-point statistics do not fully capture information from nonlinear gravitational evolution, galaxy bias, and redshift-space distortions present in galaxy redshift surveys, motivating the need for flexible, computationally efficient alternatives.
AI.method: Introduction of the augmented correlation function framework where an arbitrary transformation of the galaxy field defines additional latent dimensions extending the standard two-point correlation function. Specifically, a latent variable based on the pairwise gradient of the inverse Laplacian of the galaxy density field is studied to isolate clustering regimes.
AI.result: The augmented correlation function distinguishes clustering regimes related to infalling and outflowing pairs, and Fisher forecasts using $z=1$ halo catalogues from Quijote simulations in $νΛ	ext{CDM}$ cosmology show systematically tighter constraints on all cosmological parameters considered.
AI.conclusion: The augmented correlation function framework demonstrates potential as a flexible and computationally efficient tool to extract additional cosmological information beyond standard two-point statistics from spectroscopic galaxy surveys, although further validation beyond Fisher forecasts is needed due to the exploratory nature of the analysis.

title: The Northern Cross Fast Radio Burst project: VI. The INCART public database
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in PASA. INCART is available here: https://ngc-frb-incart.ira.inaf.it/
summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are bright (Jansky-level) and short-duration ($\sim 1$ ms) flashes of extragalactic origin. Observations of single events have now been complemented by large-area surveys, delivering FRB catalogues and enabling the first population studies. The Northern Cross (NC) radio interferometer is one of the instruments performing observations of FRBs. In this work, we present the Italian Northern Cross Atlas of Radio Transients ({\tt INCART}), a public platform for the distribution of data products from the NC. {\tt INCART} makes available to the community the FRBs observed by the NC through manageable frequency-time series datasets and catalogues with best-fit physical parameters. The design of {\tt INCART} guarantees the possibility of scientific re-analysis of the FRB properties, in view also of future releases of the processing pipeline. Furthermore, {\tt INCART} focuses on long-term storage optimisation, which is a key aspect of state-of-the-art instrumentation. Public access to the FRB data from the NC maximises the legacy value of the collection, facilitates the synergy with other publicly-available catalogues, and fosters research group collaborations.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces INCART, a public platform distributing Northern Cross radio interferometer FRB data sets and catalogues, enabling population studies and collaborative research with optimized long-term data storage.
AI.motivation: To enable population studies of fast radio bursts (FRBs) by providing accessible, well-organized observational data from the Northern Cross (NC) radio interferometer.
AI.method: Development of the Italian Northern Cross Atlas of Radio Transients (INCART), a public platform distributing frequency-time series datasets and catalogues with best-fit physical parameters of FRBs detected by the NC.
AI.result: INCART offers publicly accessible FRB data from NC with support for scientific re-analysis, long-term storage optimization, and compatibility with future pipeline updates, thereby enhancing data legacy and collaborative research.
AI.conclusion: The publicly available INCART platform from the NC facilitates FRB population studies, maximizes data legacy, and promotes collaboration by providing well-structured, long-term archived FRB data.

title: Long-Duration GRB 211211A: Internal Energy Dissipation Driven by a Long-Lived Magnetar
comment: 15 pages, 4 figures. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: The most promising candidate for short-duration gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) is the merger of two neutron stars (NSs), which produces kilonovae (KNe) in the aftermath. This merging can result in a fast-spinning, highly magnetic NS, known as a millisecond magnetar, whose accretion processes can explain different phases in GRBs. The identification of a KN associated with the atypical long-duration GRB 211211A contradicted the classification schemes of the GRB progenitors. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of gamma- and X-ray observations, focusing on modeling X-ray data from a long-lived magnetar with two distinct fallback accretion rates ($\dot{M}\propto t^0$ and $\propto t^{\frac12}$) during the initial phase. The internal energy dissipation of the magnetar spin-down power, through the magnetization parameter, accounts for the long duration of the prompt gamma-ray episode observed in GRB 211211A. Furthermore, we provide a satisfactory explanation for the precursor and extended emissions following the prompt episode within the magnetar model with two fallback accretion rates. Although these accretion rates explain different characteristics, the model that incorporates a variable accretion rate offers a more accurate description. The current scenario for the GRB 211211A observations aligns with a compact binary merger that produces a long-lived magnetar instead of an immediate black hole.

AI.tldr: This study models the atypical long-duration GRB 211211A's gamma and X-ray emissions as arising from a long-lived millisecond magnetar formed after a neutron star merger, using fallback accretion rates to explain its complex emission phases, thereby resolving classification contradictions and supporting a magnetar central engine scenario.
AI.motivation: To resolve the contradiction in GRB classification caused by detecting a kilonova associated with the atypical long-duration GRB 211211A and provide a coherent model explaining its emission features.
AI.method: Analysis of gamma- and X-ray data from GRB 211211A, modeling X-ray emission based on a long-lived millisecond magnetar with two fallback accretion rate models ($\dot{M}\propto t^0$ and $\propto t^{1/2}$), and considering internal energy dissipation via magnetar spin-down power and magnetization parameter.
AI.result: The magnetar model with two fallback accretion rates successfully explains the prompt gamma-ray emission duration, precursor, and extended emissions of GRB 211211A. The variable fallback accretion rate model provides a more accurate fit, supporting a scenario where a compact binary merger produces a long-lived magnetar rather than an immediate black hole.
AI.conclusion: The observations of GRB 211211A are consistent with a compact binary neutron star merger forming a long-lived millisecond magnetar, challenging traditional GRB progenitor classifications and explaining the observed emission phases through magnetar spin-down and fallback accretion dynamics.

title: A new completely parameter-free clustering algorithm for unsupervised classification of BATSE gamma-ray bursts
summary: Cluster analysis is a widely applied machine learning technique to understand the existing patterns in the population of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), in order to explore their physical sources. In the present scenario, the number of clusters corresponding to differentiable groups is still under conflict, in spite of numerous attempts with the state-of-the-art clustering procedures. This crucial unknown parameter needs to be evaluated, either directly or indirectly in terms of other tuning parameters, to produce the clusters in GRBs through implementation of an appropriate clustering algorithm. While most of the applied algorithms reached two physically explained groups of merger and collapsar predominated by the short and long bursts respectively, other statistical approaches violated this binary partition. However, physical establishment of any additional cluster(s) is not yet confirmed. Therefore, we propose a new algorithm, from a different stream of clustering referred to as `completely parameter-free', which carries out the classification of GRBs in a manner that has not been tried so far. It indicates two main groups, of short and long duration bursts from the BATSE sample, compatible with the merger-collapsar theory.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new parameter-free clustering algorithm that classifies gamma-ray bursts into two main groups, short and long, consistent with existing physical theories, resolving previous conflicts in cluster determination.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to resolve the ongoing conflict regarding the number of distinguishable clusters in gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) populations, which is crucial to understanding their physical sources.
AI.method: A novel clustering algorithm from a completely parameter-free clustering approach was proposed, contrasting previous state-of-the-art methods that required tuning parameters.
AI.result: The new algorithm indicates two main groups of GRBs—short and long duration bursts—from the BATSE sample, aligning with the merger-collapsar theory.
AI.conclusion: The study confirms that a completely parameter-free clustering method can effectively classify GRBs into two physically meaningful groups without prior parameter tuning, supporting the traditional binary partition of merger and collapsar GRBs.
